chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — regarding
an egg that came out from (the body of) a dead chicken. So he said: 'If the egg has acquired the hard shell, then there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الْجِلْد الْغَلِيظ: The hard/thick shell — the outer calcified shell of an egg, indicating the egg has fully developed; a legal criterion distinguishing a complete egg from an incompletely formed one
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: No harm/no problem — a standard jurisprudential phrase indicating permissibility, commonly used by the Imams to signal that an act or object is halal
key_terms.مَيْتَة: Carrion/dead animal — an animal that died without lawful slaughter; its flesh is ritually impure (najis) and forbidden to consume

ai.seo_question: Is an egg from a dead chicken halal according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about eggs extracted from the body of a dead chicken. He ruled that if such an egg has already formed its hard outer shell, it is permissible to use. This ruling reflects the principle in Shia jurisprudence that an egg which has fully formed its protective casing is considered a separate entity from the dead animal and is not made impure (najis) by its origin.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding
eggs extracted from the dead chicken. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the egg as the hard shell, so there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “About the case of an egg which comes out of the bottom of a dead chicken, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If the egg is covered with its thick crust , then it is not unlawful.’”
